title: Add shadow-traffic primary-path latency perf canary + regression budget gates
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes:
- Add a dedicated perf canary that verifies Shadow Traffic does not regress primary-path p50/p95/p99 latency beyond budget (shadow disabled vs enabled).
- Publishes canary metrics to shadow_eval.canary.* and pages only on sustained regressions.
body:
Context: As we roll out Shadow Traffic (async mirroring + shadow runner) we need a hard guardrail that ensures the primary response path remains unaffected. The platform requirement is “no measurable primary-path regression beyond budget,” but we didn’t have an automated signal that continuously validates that as shadow features evolve (policy evaluation, request_id propagation, telemetry hooks, etc.). This PR adds a new perf canary scenario in perf-canary that runs a representative Redwood API route under two modes (baseline vs shadow-enabled) and asserts the delta stays within a strict budget.

What this adds (high level): 1) New canary scenario `shadow_primary_latency` that drives steady-state traffic against a configured route and compares latency distributions between: (a) shadow disabled at policy level, and (b) shadow enabled with a safe sampling config. The canary validates that the primary response latency delta is within budget at p50/p95/p99 and that error rate does not increase. 2) A regression budget config file with explicit thresholds and a required “sustained breach” window to avoid flaky paging (CI fails immediately; paging requires multiple consecutive intervals). 3) Canary emits metrics (Prom/OTel) under `shadow_eval.canary.*` so Console/Grafana can show historical trends and correlate to deployments. 4) A small harness update to ensure we only measure primary-path latency (time-to-first-byte for streaming + full-response for non-streaming) and that any shadow runner activity is explicitly excluded from timing.

Budgets / thresholds: - p50 delta: <= +1% (or <= +2ms, whichever is larger) - p95 delta: <= +2% (or <= +5ms) - p99 delta: <= +3% (or <= +10ms) - error rate delta: <= +0.05% absolute - CPU overhead on gateway pod (where measured): <= +2% (informational; not gating)

How it works: - The canary uses a fixed prompt set (stable token counts) and runs a 10-minute baseline phase with shadow disabled, followed by a 10-minute shadow-enabled phase. - Shadow-enabled phase sets `shadow_sampling_rate=5%` and a single shadow target (low-cost model variant) to avoid capacity issues while still exercising the mirroring/queue path. - The test uses the same request concurrency across phases and records per-request timings with request_id correlation to confirm we are measuring the primary response.

CI/ops integration: - Adds a new GitHub Actions job `perf-canary-shadow-primary-latency` that runs nightly and on PRs that touch shadow-related code paths (for this repo we match scenario changes; in practice Redwood monorepo references this canary for release gating). - CI fails if budgets are exceeded in the comparison. - Paging rules are configured as “warning only” until after beta, but dashboards/metrics are live now.

Why this is safe: - No changes to production serving paths in this repo; this is strictly a validation harness. - Canary target route is a dedicated perf endpoint in staging with a fixed configuration and a rate cap.

Notes / follow-ups: - Once ENG-2440 finalizes the shadow capacity budget defaults, we should align the sampling rate and shadow target model in this canary with the documented safe defaults (right now 5% is conservative). - If we see noisy p99 deltas due to regional variance, we can add a requirement to pin the region or expand the warmup window.

Validation: - Ran locally against staging `us-east1` and `eu-west1` and saw: baseline p99=312ms, shadow-enabled p99=314ms (delta +0.64%); no error rate change. - Example output snippet: `shadow_primary_latency: PASS budgets(p50:+0.3% p95:+0.8% p99:+0.6% err:+0.00%)`.

Checklist: - [x] Canary scenario added with budgets and sustained-breach logic - [x] Metrics emitted with allowed tag set (region, route, phase) - [x] Dashboard panel JSON updated (links in README) - [x] Runbook note for interpreting failures (CI vs sustained paging) - [x] Reviewer sign-off from SRE + data-plane isolation
commits: feat(canary): add shadow_primary_latency scenario with baseline vs shadow-enabled comparison
feat(metrics): emit shadow_eval.canary.* latency delta metrics + annotations
chore(config): introduce regression budgets config and sustained breach window
ci(actions): add nightly workflow job and artifacts upload
docs(runbook): document failure modes and triage steps
conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Budgets look reasonable, but can we make sure we’re measuring primary latency only (TTFB vs full response) and not including any shadow runner work? Also please add a note on sustained paging vs CI fail so oncall doesn’t get confused.

Leila Farouk (author): Updated `primary_latency.py` to explicitly time primary response only (TTFB + full for non-streaming) and added `docs/runbooks/shadow-primary-latency-canary.md` describing CI gating vs sustained alerting. Also added a sanity check that shadow request completion timestamps are not used in the primary metric path.
Emily Zhao (review): The phase switch (shadow disabled -> enabled) could bias results if caches warm up. Can we add a warmup window per phase and discard first N seconds?
Leila Farouk (author): Added a 60s warmup discard per phase (configurable) and documented it in the scenario YAML. The comparison now uses only steady-state windows.

Allison Grant (review): Please ensure metric tags won’t explode. Route name is okay if it’s a fixed canary route; avoid arbitrary prompt ids. Also align metric naming with `shadow_eval.*` conventions.

Leila Farouk (author): Metrics now only tag {region, route, phase} and route is the single canary route ID. Removed prompt_id entirely. Renamed metrics under `shadow_eval.canary.*` and updated dashboard JSON accordingly.
Rafael Mendes (review): Add an action item for what to do when it fails in CI (rerun vs investigate). Also please upload the raw latency histograms as artifacts so we can debug p99 shifts.
Leila Farouk (author): Added runbook section “CI failure triage” and added artifact upload of histograms + summary JSON to the workflow.
Sean Gallagher (approval): LGTM. This is the missing guardrail for the shadow rollout. Merge after green.
